problem: Which of the following **cannot** be the slope field for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(y)?$
worked_solution:
Notice that we are given an equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(y).
$$

This is an autonomous equation because the right-hand side is a function of $y$ only. This means that, for a fixed value of $y,$ the slope does not vary with $x.$ 

Of the given slope fields, the only one that varies with $x$ for a fixed value of $y$ is the following:

  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040222/assets/9f883ac23f1a6574f2afdf2ca4dcb0aaf617c992c6c67f34ca5d3a0af63b8149.png)

 

To see this more clearly, notice that if we draw a horizontal line, the slopes touching the line vary as we go left and right along the line. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040222/assets/b157285c42bd83c28ed4b3da51fa6d0e83353ae806781fd4231abd45da880228.png)
